title: PowerGeometryRelativeErrorConvex.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a differentiable convex function f:E→ℝ with globally L-Lipschitz derivative in the dual norm. A global minimizer x⋆ exists with ‖x⋆−x0‖≤R. No strong convexity is assumed.

oracle.label: inexact_gradient
oracle.details: Each query x returns a continuous linear functional g satisfying ‖g−Df(x)‖≤α‖Df(x)‖ for every call index, seed, and query. Function values are not supplied. The budget counts individual derivative-oracle calls.

distinctive_assumptions.label: relative_error
distinctive_assumptions.details: The public error level satisfies 0≤α≤1/4. The error is bounded pointwise relative to the true derivative's dual norm; it need not be unbiased, independent, or identically distributed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: non_euclidean_geometry
distinctive_assumptions.details: The norm need not arise from an inner product. For public p>2 and c>0, ψ(x)=‖x−x0‖²/2 is differentiable and satisfies Dψ(y,x)≥c‖y−x‖^p/(‖y−x0‖+‖x−x0‖)^(p−2) for all x,y, where Dψ(y,x)=ψ(y)−ψ(x)−Dψ(x)[y−x].

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real normed vector space; no particular dimension or coordinate norm is prescribed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E, its geometry, L>0, α, p, c, and x0 are public. R≥0 and ε>0 determine the external oracle budget but are not supplied to makeAlgorithm. The objective and minimizer are hidden.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/PowerGeometryRelativeErrorConvex.lean: Public, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.valid; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The returned point x must satisfy f(x)−f(x⋆)≤ε for a global minimizer x⋆, after the prescribed fixed oracle budget.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The objective-gap guarantee holds almost surely under the product of the algorithm's seed law and the oracle's joint seed law; it is not merely an expectation bound.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup combines pointwise relative derivative errors with a specific power-type Bregman lower bound for the squared norm, and requires almost-sure objective accuracy under a fixed budget without exposing R or ε to the algorithm.

descriptionHtml:
Power Geometry with Relative Errors

We consider minimizing a differentiable convex function f:E→R on a finite-dimensional real normed space E. Its derivative Df is L-Lipschitz, with L>0. At a given point x0∈E, the squared norm is differentiable and satisfies a power-type curvature bound with exponent p>2 and constant c>0. A global minimizer x⋆ satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R, where R≥0. The oracle returns a dual vector g with ∥g−Df(x)∥op≤α∥Df(x)∥op at x, where 0≤α≤1/4. For ε>0, the goal is f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely for an output x¯∈E under the joint law of algorithm and oracle randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). Write E∗ for the continuous dual of E and ∥⋅∥op for its induced operator norm. Define ψ(x)=12∥x−x0∥2. The algorithm receives E, L, α, p, c, and x0; the radius R and tolerance ε may enter only the oracle-call budget.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Power geometry). The function ψ is Fréchet differentiable everywhere, and for every x,y∈E, c∥y−x∥p(∥y−x0∥+∥x−x0∥)p−2≤ψ(y)−ψ(x)−Dψ(x)[y−x]. The fraction is defined to be zero when x=y=x0.

Assumption 2 (Convexity and smoothness). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere. For every x,y∈E and t∈[0,1], f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y),∥Df(x)−Df(y)∥op≤L∥x−y∥.

Assumption 3 (Initial distance). There exists x⋆∈E such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈E,∥x⋆−x0∥≤R.

Assumption 4 (Relative-error oracle). Queries may be made at any point x∈E. Every oracle reply g∈E∗ satisfies ∥g−Df(x)∥op≤α∥Df(x)∥op. This bound holds for every query history and every realization of the oracle randomness. Replies may depend on the history, and oracle randomness across calls may be dependent. The algorithm’s randomness is independent of the oracle randomness.

After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯∈E must satisfy f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤εP-a.s., where P is the joint law of the algorithm and oracle randomness, and x⋆ is a fixed global minimizer.

comparisonHtml:
In a finite-dimensional real normed space, f is differentiable and convex, ∥Df(x)−Df(y)∥∗≤L∥x−y∥, and a global minimizer satisfies ∥x∗−x0∥≤R. Here L,c>0, p>2, R≥0, and 0≤α≤1/4. The differentiable function ψ(x)=∥x−x0∥2/2 satisfies Dψ(y,x)≥c∥y−x∥p/(∥y−x0∥+∥x−x0∥)p−2 for all x,y (zero at x=y=x0). Every oracle reply obeys ∥g−Df(x)∥∗≤α∥Df(x)∥∗, allowing biased, call-dependent errors. Target: f(xK)−f(x∗)≤ε, ε>0, almost surely under every execution law; the constructed squared-norm dual-averaging output satisfies it for every seed.

(1): extends to biased relative error; matches the exact-gradient rate for fixed p. Updates need neither R, ε, nor horizon; the stopping budget still does. (1) has larger p-dependent constants; on ℓpd, C=p(p−1)27(p−2)/2 (1536 at p=4).
(3) Derived bound: (Vasin and Gasnikov 2026), Thm. 7.2

⋅[1+log⁡(d2sT)]) gradient calls. On ℓpd via Euclidean conversion, with d2sT>1 and dsα≤1/3.

 (1): dimension-free; for fixed p and d≳Tp/(p+2), removes dimension factors and logarithm, with α2T instead of αd3sT. At p=4, d=T2, α=T−1/6≤1/4: O(1+T2/3); (3) is inapplicable. (1) loses at α=0, fixed p,d, T→∞: Tp/(p+2) versus T(1+log⁡T). At d=1, excludes 1/4<α≤1/3.
(4) SODA (Pethick 2026), Cor. 3.2 Op,τq(1+Tp/(p+2)+(σqR/ε)p) stochastic-gradient calls, one per step. On ℓpd: unbiased gradients with q-moment gradient variation (Assumptions 3–4); expected objective gap ≤ε. (1): matches the rate on the exact-gradient overlap; removes R from updates. Covers arbitrary relative bias with pathwise accuracy; no stochastic-rate comparison outside that overlap. (1) does not cover additive heavy-tailed noise allowed by (4); the noisy oracle models are incomparable.

Op permits constants depending on fixed p. In (4), q=p/(p−1); σq and τq≥1 are the additive scale and multiplicative factor in the Lq gradient-variation bound; Op,τq permits dependence on these subscripts.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Real

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.PowerGeometryRelativeErrorConvex

open OracleTemplate

structure Public where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : NormedSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  L : ℝ
  α : ℝ
  p : ℝ
  c : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.linearE Public.finiteE

noncomputable def Public.ψ (d : Public) (x : d.E) : ℝ := ‖x - d.x0‖ ^ 2 / 2

def Public.Valid (d : Public) : Prop :=
  0 < d.L ∧ 2 < d.p ∧ 0 < d.c ∧ 0 ≤ d.α ∧ d.α ≤ 1 / 4 ∧
  (∀ x, DifferentiableAt ℝ d.ψ x) ∧
  (∀ x y, d.c * ‖y - x‖ ^ d.p /
    (‖y - d.x0‖ + ‖x - d.x0‖) ^ (d.p - 2) ≤
      d.ψ y - d.ψ x - fderiv ℝ d.ψ x (y - x))

structure Params where
  data : Public
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance d := d.E → ℝ
  Query d := d.E
  Reply d := d.E →L[ℝ] ℝ
  Output d := d.E
  publicInput q := q.data
  valid q := q.data.Valid ∧ 0 ≤ q.R ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f oracle :=
    (∀ x, HasFDerivAt f (fderiv ℝ f x) x) ∧
    ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ f ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖fderiv ℝ f x - fderiv ℝ f y‖ ≤ q.data.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∀ k seed x, ‖oracle.answer k (0, x) seed - fderiv ℝ f x‖ ≤
      q.data.α * ‖fderiv ℝ f x‖) ∧
    (∃ xstar, (∀ x, f xstar ≤ f x) ∧ ‖xstar - q.data.x0‖ ≤ q.R)
  successful q f output P :=
    ∃ xstar, (∀ x, f xstar ≤ f x) ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure _), f (output ω) - f xstar ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.PowerGeometryRelativeErrorConvex
